threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think saying 'sorry' when bumping into people is polite. Here, it’s just part of the daily shuffle.
Last week on the 36, I saw a guy trying to barter with the driver using a pack of gum and a half-eaten sandwich. Driver just shook his head and smiled.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I once saw a guy in a full suit casually arguing with a pigeon over a dropped kebab. That's when I knew Neukölln had a character all its own.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a U-Bahn stop named after a famous Turkish poet, with its walls covered in poetry murals that change every few months.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by how they size up BART delays; if they roll their eyes and check their watch, they’ve been through this grind before.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a full tuxedo, top hat included, hop on the 47. He held the door for a lady with a small dog, like it was a wedding procession.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is just about the vibrant squares, but miss the subtle charm of the narrow alleys, where real life unfolds away from the crowds.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by how they still struggle to order a simple 'café con leche' without fumbling the accent.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'the Tube' and not 'the Overground'—big mistake! You'll hear locals drop the 'Tube' like it’s a holiday train.
Last night on the 77 bus, a guy serenaded the driver with classic soul tunes. Didn't have a clue he was belting it out. Only in Brixton!

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw kids using the U-Bahn as their personal playground—jumping between carriages, giggling like it was a carnival ride.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You can hop a U-Bahn and find a spontaneous street party on any Saturday night in Kreuzberg—where else can you find a club underground and above ground at the same time?

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know you're local when you can guess the BART delays by the time of day, yet still get annoyed when a stop is closed unexpectedly.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy on the bus serenading the passengers with an accordion. The whole ride turned from dreary to a spontaneous concert. Classic Tenderloin.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think they can grab a coffee and sit for hours; in Gràcia, locals down their café con leche and dash to work. It's a quick sip, not a long sit.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell when someone’s new if they’re still amazed by the 'free' tapas with drinks at the bars. The locals expect it, but fresh faces are always snapping selfies with their plates.
